philosophy: Two minute tempo is used at the end of the half and when trailing at the end of the game.
Personnel is 11 unless told otherwise.
The count is Turbo. With crowd noise it moves to Center One.
The sideline gives the first formation and play. With the clock running the QB calls everything after that.
Any no huddle package (Rollin for example) can be the base.
The QB tells the line and back the run or protection out loud, then signals the tight end and receivers by hand.
Know the half, the time left, whether a touchdown or a field goal is needed, and how many timeouts remain. For a field goal the head coach gives the yard line the kicker needs.
All timeouts come from the sideline.
Everyone relays the call. Be sure of the calls and signals.
Move fast without rushing. Nobody needs to make a hero play, just do the job.
Know the down. The QB never spikes it on fourth down.
The QB runs only for big yards or to get out of bounds.
Time beats yards. Do not fight for inches: secure the ball, go down, and get set. Still know when the chains have to move on third and fourth down.
After the play, put the ball on the inside edge of the hash fast. Never throw it to the official.
On or outside the numbers, get out of bounds going forward. Going out sideways or backwards does not stop the clock.
Caught inside the numbers with no way out, turn upfield and get down.

The clock starts on the whistle, not the snap, after a measurement where the ball stayed in bounds, after an official's timeout for technical reasons, after an offensive penalty in the last minute, and after a booth challenge where the ball stayed in bounds.
Any ball carrier can give himself up so the offense can call timeout or spike it. Players are told before the play when that applies.
Backs: a blitz is likely right after the clock stops. The protection job comes first. Run sharp routes, there are yards underneath when the defense protects deep.
Line: stunts and games are coming. Climb out of piles and get set fast.
Down-Down Timeout: 6 to 11 seconds left and yards matter. After the catch or run the ball carrier slides feet first, and the sideline calls timeout as soon as he is down.
Down-Down Clock: 12 to 17 seconds left. Same slide, then everyone sprints to Double Rt Off ready for the Clock call.

Down-Down Mayday: 18 or more seconds left, running a third down play with no timeouts and no spike available on fourth down. Same slide, then get off the field sideways so the field goal unit can get on.

concepts.summary: One sideline shot: Trout Rt 2 Scat Layers X Bench. The X runs a Bench, a deep sideline route at 18 to 20 yards, the F a deep sail at 12 to 15, the H a flat at 3 to 5, and the Z a go at 20 to 25 as the alert. Deep pressure is the alert note on the line.
concepts.progression: 1 X Bench, 2 F deep sail, 3 Y, as best read. The Z go is an alert.
concepts.qb: Alert the go against deep pressure.
concepts.hb: Flat at 3 to 5 yards from the Scat release.

concepts.summary: Three plays for the Down-Down situations. Brawlin Spear: a push and widen dagger at 8 yards with a deep dagger at 18 to 20, a slam, a blink alert and a yes/no at 20, with a check wide outlet. Double Rt Close A 300 Scram Lions: three step slants everywhere, split four yards wider to the boundary and two to the field or middle, inside slants from the inside men. Swift Rt Tout Tres 3 Scrabble Samurai: a far cross at 22 to 25, a lick flat at 3 to 5, a rib shallow, a low cross and a widen dagger at 10 to 12.
concepts.progression: Spear: 1 dagger, 2 dagger pivot, as best read. Lions: 1 and 2 the outside slants, 3 the inside slant. Samurai: 1 widen dagger, 2 far cross, 3 lick flat, 4 rib shallow, 5 low cross, as best read.

positions.Z: Push and widen dagger at 8 yards (Spear); slant; far cross at 22 to 25 (Samurai).
positions.F: Dagger at 18 to 20 (Spear); slant; lick flat at 3 to 5 (Samurai).
positions.X: Yes/no at 20 (Spear); slant; low cross at 20 (Samurai).
positions.H: Check wide outlet (Spear); inside slant; widen dagger at 10 to 12 (Samurai).

alerts: Lions splits: plus 4 to the boundary, plus 2 to the field or middle.

concepts.summary: Four end of game plays. Gun Bunch Rt Extend Tite 3 Jet Stay Hail Mary: a jumper, a front tip and a back tip, with the QB able to call go. Double Rt Close A 3 Scram 5 Verts (can) Curry: five verticals with a middle clear, routes to the goal line, the back helping left, Y and F making a you/me call against a bump, scramble rules when the play breaks down, and Curry as the quick screen check. West Rt Acer Center Rt: a tight zone play used to burn time and center the ball for a field goal, with the H set at 3 yards opposite the wing behind the guard to clean up any leak, and the QB getting to the line fast, centering and kneeling on a count of one. West Rt Tighter Boot Rt Foul Ball: fourth down with 6 seconds or less, when a punt could be blocked, the QB rolls right and throws the ball away deep along the right sideline while the wide receiver runs a go on a max split and everyone else protects.
concepts.qb: Hail Mary: go call from the QB. 5 Verts: run the routes to win, scramble rules off schedule. Center Rt: hurry to the line, center the ball, take a knee. Foul Ball: roll right and throw it away deep along the sideline.
concepts.hb: 5 Verts: help left. Center Rt: H aligns at 3 yards opposite the wing behind the guard and secures leakage to the edge.

positions.X: Front tip (Hail Mary); go to the goal line (5 Verts); go on a max split plus 4 (Foul Ball).
positions.Y: Front tip (Hail Mary); you/me call with F against a bump (5 Verts).
positions.F: Back tip (Hail Mary); middle clear, Save 2, end zone plus 3 (5 Verts).
positions.OL: Tight zone on Center Rt. Protection on Foul Ball.

alerts: Center Rt can go right or left.
Foul Ball is for 6 seconds or less on fourth down.
concepts.can: 5 Verts can be checked to Curry.

concepts.summary: Victory ends the game on a knee when the downs cover the clock. The snap comes with 2 seconds on the play clock, the QB steps back once and kneels, and 2 to 4 seconds run off. Both backs walk up into the A gaps with their eyes on the exchange, the line wedges and expects contact, and the Z plays deep safety 7 yards behind the QB watching the ball and never moving up. Victory Sneak is for a backed up end of half or game when there is no room to kneel: the QB sneaks through the soft A gap, the backs push the pile, and the Z sits at 5 yards.
concepts.qb: Snap at 2 seconds on the play clock. Victory: one step back and kneel. Sneak: go through the soft A gap.
concepts.hb: Both backs up in the A gaps either side of the QB, eyes on the snap. On the Sneak, push the pile.

positions.Z: Deep safety behind the QB, 7 yards on Victory and 5 on Victory Sneak. Eyes on the ball, do not move toward the line.

alerts: Expect a 2 to 4 second run off per play.

concepts.summary: Spike to stop the clock when giving up a down is worth it. The QB shouts Clock Clock over and over, everyone sprints to the ball and sets in a legal formation from Double Rt Off: line shoe to shoe in a two point stance, skill players facing forward, outside receivers on the ball and inside receivers off.
concepts.qb: Yell Clock Clock repeatedly, get set, spike it.

positions.OL: Shoe to shoe, two point stance.

concepts.summary: 911 is the last play with the clock running, no timeouts and no time to spike: Double Rt Off 3 Jet Aggie on Turbo. Three seams bend at 10 to 12 yards against two safeties and break to open grass, the outside men run go routes on a max split, and releases and spacing decide it. Aggie is the 2x2 name, Dancer the 3x1. Sticky is for beating a challenge flag: Snug Rt 300 Jet X and Z Stick Thru on Set Hut, sticks at 5 yards, flats at 2 to 3, and a check thru outlet at 3. For a shot in that spot the call is Swoosh Swoosh, Snug Rt 3 Jet Swoosh, with the same mechanics.
concepts.qb: 911 on Turbo. Sticky on Set Hut. Swoosh Swoosh for the shot.
concepts.hb: Sticky: check thru and outlet at 3 yards.

positions.X: Go on a max split plus 4 (911); Stick at 5 (Sticky).
positions.Z: Go on a max split plus 4 (911); Stick at 5 (Sticky).
positions.Y: Seam, bend at 10 to 12 (911); flat at 2 to 3 (Sticky).
positions.F: Seam, bend at 10 to 12 (911); flat at 2 to 3 (Sticky).

alerts: Against two safeties the seams bend at 10 to 12 yards and break to daylight.
Aggie is the 2x2 word, Dancer the 3x1.

concepts.summary: With 5 to 10 seconds left and a shot play called, the QB signals Omaha to the outside receiver when he has free access. That receiver runs a 5 yard Omaha, catches it and gets out of bounds with enough time left for one more play.
concepts.qb: Signal Omaha to the outside receiver against free access.

positions.X: Omaha at 5 yards when signaled, then out of bounds.
positions.Z: Omaha at 5 yards when signaled, then out of bounds.
